REGISTERED LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP — REGISTRATION PROCEDURE AND LIABILITY SHIELD INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme & Associates LLP

PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet, prepared by Jordan Lee, states what California's Uniform Partnership Act of 1994 provides about two specific questions: (1) the procedure a partnership follows to register with the California Secretary of State as a registered limited liability partnership, under Cal. Corp. Code § 16953, and (2) the extent — and the express statutory limits — of the liability shield that registration creates for a partner, under Cal. Corp. Code § 16306. Where a specific partnership is named below, it is Acme & Associates LLP; this sheet can also be read on its own, without that field filled in, as a general reference to what these two statutes provide. This sheet does not address which professions may lawfully use the registered limited liability partnership form in the first place; that separate eligibility question is addressed in this project's Professional LLC Prohibition in California — Information Sheet, in its clause on the registered limited liability partnership's narrower list of eligible professions, and is not restated here. This sheet states the law; it does not evaluate whether any particular partnership's registration is complete or correctly filed, whether a particular partner's conduct falls inside or outside the shield, or what a specific partnership or partner should do about either question, and it is not a substitute for individualized legal advice.

REGISTRATION PROCEDURE: WHAT MUST BE FILED WITH THE SECRETARY OF STATE
California's Uniform Partnership Act of 1994 states, in Cal. Corp. Code § 16953(a), what a partnership must file with the Secretary of State to become a registered limited liability partnership: "a registration, executed by one or more partners authorized to execute a registration," stating the partnership's name; the street address of its principal office; the mailing address of its principal office, if different from the street address; the name and street address of the agent for service of process on the partnership in California; "a brief statement of the business in which the partnership engages"; any other matters the partnership determines to include; and a statement that the partnership is registering as a registered limited liability partnership. Subdivision (b) states that "[t]he registration shall be accompanied by a fee as set forth in subdivision (a) of Section 12189 of the Government Code," and subdivision (c) states the corresponding duty on the Secretary of State's side: the Secretary of State "shall register as a registered limited liability partnership any partnership that submits a completed registration with the required fee." Read together, subdivisions (a) through (c) describe registration as a filing-based act: a partnership becomes registered by submitting these stated items and the fee, and the statute's own text does not add, as part of this filing step, any separate substantive eligibility screening by the Secretary of State beyond completeness of the registration and payment of the fee.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(a) To become a registered limited liability partnership, a partnership, other than a limited partnership, shall file with the Secretary of State a registration, executed by one or more partners authorized to execute a registration, stating all of the following: (1) The name of the partnership. (2) The street address of its principal office. (3) The mailing address of its principal office, if different from the street address. (4) The name and street address of the agent for service of process on the limited liability partnership in California in accordance with subdivision (a) of Section 16309. (5) A brief statement of the business in which the partnership engages. (6) Any other matters that the partnership determines to include. (7) That the partnership is registering as a registered limited liability partnership."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 16953(a), Uniform Partnership Act of 1994, required contents of a registered limited liability partnership registration (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=16953.)
  "(b) The registration shall be accompanied by a fee as set forth in subdivision (a) of Section 12189 of the Government Code. (c) The Secretary of State shall register as a registered limited liability partnership any partnership that submits a completed registration with the required fee."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 16953(b)-(c), Uniform Partnership Act of 1994, registration fee requirement and the Secretary of State's registration duty (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=16953.)
  Known gap: This clause states only what Cal. Corp. Code § 16953(a)-(c) itself requires to be filed and what it states the Secretary of State does upon a completed filing; it does not address separate content that the same section addresses elsewhere, including the profession-specific state-board or agency filing and registration requirements referenced in § 16953(h), or the Secretary of State's fee-cancellation process in § 16953(d) — those are outside this clause's scope. This clause also does not address which professions are eligible to register as a registered limited liability partnership in the first place; that question is addressed by this project's separate Professional LLC Prohibition in California — Information Sheet, in its clause on the registered limited liability partnership's narrower list of eligible professions (citing Cal. Corp. Code §§ 16951 and 16101), which this clause cross-references rather than restates. All three quoted subdivisions below are drawn from the single statutory section Cal. Corp. Code § 16953 and are treated as one primary source, not as independent citations of separate sections. As of this verification, the California Legislative Information website listed a single current version of Section 16953 on file, last amended by Stats. 2022, Ch. 617, Sec. 111 (effective January 1, 2023), with no competing amended version found for the same statutory year. This is one state's statute, used as evidence of what that state's law provides for this specific registration procedure — not a claim about which state's law governs any specific partnership's registration, and registration procedures vary by state. This document is informational only: it does not itself register any partnership and does not determine whether a specific partnership's filing is complete or properly executed.

WHEN REGISTRATION TAKES EFFECT, HOW LONG IT CONTINUES, AND THE STATUTE'S OWN 'OPTIONAL SECURITY REQUIREMENT' LANGUAGE
Cal. Corp. Code § 16953(e) states when registration takes effect and how long it lasts: "[a] partnership becomes a registered limited liability partnership at the time of the filing of the initial registration with the Secretary of State or at any later date or time specified in the registration and the payment of the fee required by subdivision (b)," and it "continues as a registered limited liability partnership until a notice that it is no longer a registered limited liability partnership has been filed pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 16954 or, if applicable, until it has been dissolved and finally wound up." Section 16953's own text does not state, within this subdivision, any separate requirement to periodically re-register or renew the registration itself in order for it to continue — continuation instead runs until an affirmative notice of withdrawal is filed or the partnership dissolves and winds up. Separately, subdivision (g) states that the Secretary of State's registration form "shall include the form for confirming compliance with the optional security requirement pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 16956" — language that, on its own terms, characterizes that particular requirement as "optional" rather than as a universal precondition stated within Section 16953 itself. The same subdivision also states that the instructional materials accompanying the registration form must include a notice "that filing the registration will obligate the limited liability partnership to pay an annual tax for that taxable year to the Franchise Tax Board pursuant to Section 17948 of the Revenue and Taxation Code," and that this notice must be updated annually to state the current dollar amount.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(e) A partnership becomes a registered limited liability partnership at the time of the filing of the initial registration with the Secretary of State or at any later date or time specified in the registration and the payment of the fee required by subdivision (b). A partnership continues as a registered limited liability partnership until a notice that it is no longer a registered limited liability partnership has been filed pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 16954 or, if applicable, until it has been dissolved and finally wound up."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 16953(e), Uniform Partnership Act of 1994, when registration takes effect and how long it continues (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=16953.)
  "(g) The Secretary of State shall provide a form for a registration under subdivision (a), which shall include the form for confirming compliance with the optional security requirement pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 16956. The Secretary of State shall include with instructional materials provided in conjunction with the form for a registration under subdivision (a) a notice that filing the registration will obligate the limited liability partnership to pay an annual tax for that taxable year to the Franchise Tax Board pursuant to Section 17948 of the Revenue and Taxation Code. That notice shall be updated annually to specify the dollar amount of the tax."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 16953(g), Uniform Partnership Act of 1994, registration form's reference to an optional security requirement and the annual Franchise Tax Board notice (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=16953.)
  Known gap: This clause states only what Cal. Corp. Code § 16953(e) and (g) themselves say; it does not independently examine the separate statute those subdivisions cross-reference — Section 16956(c), which defines the substance of the "optional security requirement," and Section 16954(b), which governs the notice that a partnership is no longer registered — neither of which was independently fetched or verified as part of this pass, so this clause does not state what either of those two cross-referenced sections themselves require. The annual obligation described in subdivision (g) is a tax-filing consequence of registering (an obligation to the Franchise Tax Board under Revenue and Taxation Code § 17948), not a re-registration or renewal-of-registration requirement under Section 16953 itself; this clause does not address the Revenue and Taxation Code provision beyond what Section 16953(g) itself states about it. Both quoted subdivisions below are drawn from the single statutory section Cal. Corp. Code § 16953 and are treated as one primary source. This is one state's statute, used as evidence of what that state's law provides for this specific registration procedure — not a claim about which state's law governs any specific partnership's registration, and registration procedures vary by state. This document is informational only: it does not itself register or maintain the registration of any partnership.

THE LIABILITY SHIELD: WHAT A REGISTERED LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIP PARTNER IS NOT LIABLE FOR, SOLELY AS A PARTNER
Cal. Corp. Code § 16306(c) states the core liability rule for a registered limited liability partnership. "Notwithstanding any other section of this chapter, and subject to subdivisions (d), (e), (f), and (h), a partner in a registered limited liability partnership is not liable or accountable, directly or indirectly, including by way of indemnification, contribution, assessment, or otherwise, for debts, obligations, or liabilities of or chargeable to the partnership or another partner in the partnership, whether arising in tort, contract, or otherwise, that are incurred, created, or assumed by the partnership while the partnership is a registered limited liability partnership, by reason of being a partner or acting in the conduct of the business or activities of the partnership." This is a shield against liability that would otherwise attach to a person merely by reason of being a partner, or by reason of acting in the conduct of the partnership's business or activities — that is, against vicarious liability for the partnership's debts and for the acts of other partners and the partnership itself. The subdivision states this rule as applying "[n]otwithstanding any other section of this chapter," but expressly makes it "subject to subdivisions (d), (e), (f), and (h)" of the same section, meaning the statute's own text builds named exceptions and qualifications into the shield rather than stating it as absolute.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(c) Notwithstanding any other section of this chapter, and subject to subdivisions (d), (e), (f), and (h), a partner in a registered limited liability partnership is not liable or accountable, directly or indirectly, including by way of indemnification, contribution, assessment, or otherwise, for debts, obligations, or liabilities of or chargeable to the partnership or another partner in the partnership, whether arising in tort, contract, or otherwise, that are incurred, created, or assumed by the partnership while the partnership is a registered limited liability partnership, by reason of being a partner or acting in the conduct of the business or activities of the partnership."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 16306(c), Uniform Partnership Act of 1994, core liability shield for a partner in a registered limited liability partnership (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=16306.)
  Known gap: This clause states only what Cal. Corp. Code § 16306(c) itself says; the express limits it cross-references in subdivisions (d), (e), (f), and (h) are addressed only in part, by the separate clause of this document on the shield's limits (covering subdivisions (e) and (f)) — subdivisions (d) (a partner's ability to agree in writing to assume specified liabilities) and (h) (a partner's separate ability to act as guarantor or surety) are not covered by either clause and were not independently verified here. This clause is one subsection of the single statutory section Cal. Corp. Code § 16306; this document's separate General Partnership Agreement document already cites subdivisions (a) and (b) of the same section for the different, contrasting point that a general partnership's default rule is joint and several liability with no comparable shield, and flags subdivisions (c) through (h) as a distinct regime it does not cover — this clause is offered specifically to fill that gap for the registered limited liability partnership form, without restating that other document's content. As of this verification, the California Legislative Information website listed a single version of Section 16306 on file, dated as added by Stats. 1996, Ch. 1003, Sec. 2 (effective January 1, 1997), with no amendment or competing version found since. This clause does not evaluate whether any specific partnership is currently a registered limited liability partnership or whether a specific partner's conduct falls inside or outside this shield. This is one state's statute, used as evidence of what that state's law provides for this specific entity form — not a claim about which state's law governs any specific partnership, and liability-shield rules vary by state. This document is informational only.

THE SHIELD'S LIMITS: A PARTNER'S OWN TORTIOUS CONDUCT, AND A SEPARATE LIMIT FOR LEGAL SERVICES
The registered limited liability partnership shield described in Cal. Corp. Code § 16306(c) is not absolute; the same section states named limits on it. Subdivision (e) states: "[n]othing in subdivision (c) shall be construed to affect the liability of a partner of a registered limited liability partnership to third parties for that partner's tortious conduct." By its own terms, subdivision (c)'s shield reaches liability that would otherwise attach to a partner "by reason of being a partner or acting in the conduct of the business or activities of the partnership" — that is, liability arising from the partnership relationship itself — while subdivision (e) states that this shield does not extend to a partner's own tortious conduct toward a third party. Subdivision (f) states a separate, additionally specific limit for the practice of law: "[t]he limitation of liability in subdivision (c) shall not apply to claims based upon acts, errors, or omissions arising out of the rendering of professional limited liability partnership services of a registered limited liability partnership providing legal services unless that partnership has a currently effective certificate of registration issued by the State Bar." Read together, these two subdivisions state that the shield in subdivision (c) coexists with, rather than displaces, a partner's own liability for their own tortious conduct, and that for a law-practice registered limited liability partnership specifically, the shield itself does not apply to professional-service claims at all unless the partnership holds a currently effective State Bar certificate of registration.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(e) Nothing in subdivision (c) shall be construed to affect the liability of a partner of a registered limited liability partnership to third parties for that partner’s tortious conduct."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 16306(e), Uniform Partnership Act of 1994, limit preserving a partner's liability for that partner's own tortious conduct (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=16306.)
  "(f) The limitation of liability in subdivision (c) shall not apply to claims based upon acts, errors, or omissions arising out of the rendering of professional limited liability partnership services of a registered limited liability partnership providing legal services unless that partnership has a currently effective certificate of registration issued by the State Bar."
  — Cal. Corp. Code § 16306(f), Uniform Partnership Act of 1994, additional limit on the shield for a registered limited liability partnership providing legal services (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CORP&sectionNum=16306.)
  Known gap: The text of Cal. Corp. Code § 16306(e), as fetched and verified for this clause, states the limit in terms of "that partner's tortious conduct" toward third parties; it does not, in this subdivision or elsewhere in the section as fetched, use language expressly limiting a partner's own conduct to that partner's personal negligence, wrongful acts, or misconduct, or the negligence, wrongful acts, or misconduct of a person under that partner's direct supervision or control — no phrase resembling "direct supervision" or "control" over another person's conduct appears anywhere in the fetched text of Section 16306. A reader should not assume Section 16306 contains that more specific supervision-based formulation found in some other jurisdictions' limited liability partnership statutes; this clause states only the broader "tortious conduct" formulation that California's current text actually uses. This clause also does not address subdivision (d) (a partner's ability to agree in writing to be liable for specified debts) or subdivision (h) (a partner's separate ability to act as guarantor or surety), which are outside its scope. Both quoted subdivisions are drawn from the single statutory section Cal. Corp. Code § 16306 and are treated as one primary source, alongside the separate clause of this document quoting subdivision (c) of the same section. As of this verification, the California Legislative Information website listed a single version of Section 16306 on file, dated as added by Stats. 1996, Ch. 1003, Sec. 2, with no amendment or competing version found since. This clause does not evaluate whether any specific partner's conduct is or is not "tortious conduct" within the meaning of subdivision (e), and does not address professions other than the practice of law under subdivision (f). This is one state's statute, used as evidence of what that state's law provides — not a claim about which state's law governs any specific partner's conduct, and these rules vary by state. This document is informational only.

SIGNATURE AND CERTIFICATION
I, Jordan Lee, certify that I prepared this information sheet as a summary of Cal. Corp. Code §§ 16953 and 16306, for informational reference only. This information sheet does not constitute legal advice, does not evaluate whether any specific partnership's registration is complete or properly filed, does not evaluate whether any specific partner's conduct falls inside or outside the statutory liability shield, and is not a substitute for consulting a person licensed to practice law in the relevant jurisdiction.

Partnership name, if applicable: Acme & Associates LLP

Executed on September 5, 2026 at Oakland, California.

Signature of Jordan Lee: ☐ _________________________

Code § 16306(e), as fetched and verified for this clause, states the limit in terms of "that partner's tortious conduct" toward third parties; it does not, in this subdivision or elsewhere in the section as fetched, use language expressly limiting a partner's own conduct to that partner's personal negligence, wrongful acts, or misconduct, or the negligence, wrongful acts, or misconduct of a person under that partner's direct supervision or control — no phrase resembling "direct supervision" or "control" over another person's conduct appears anywhere in the fetched text of Section 16306. A reader should not assume Section 16306 contains that more specific supervision-based formulation found in some other jurisdictions' limited liability partnership statutes; this clause states only the broader "tortious conduct" formulation that California's current text actually uses. This clause also does not address subdivision (d) (a partner's ability to agree in writing to be liable for specified debts) or subdivision (h) (a partner's separate ability to act as guarantor or surety), which are outside its scope. Both quoted subdivisions are drawn from the single statutory section Cal. Corp. Code § 16306 and are treated as one primary source, alongside the separate clause of this document quoting subdivision (c) of the same section. As of this verification, the California Legislative Information website listed a single version of Section 16306 on file, dated as added by Stats. 1996, Ch. 1003, Sec. 2, with no amendment or competing version found since. This clause does not evaluate whether any specific partner's conduct is or is not "tortious conduct" within the meaning of subdivision (e), and does not address professions other than the practice of law under subdivision (f). This is one state's statute, used as evidence of what that state's law provides — not a claim about which state's law governs any specific partner's conduct, and these rules vary by state. This document is informational only.
